segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ יְתוֹמָה שֶׁהִשִּׂיאַתָּה אִמָּהּ אוֹ אַחֶיהָ מִדַּעְתָּהּ, וְכָתְבוּ לָהּ בְּמֵאָה אוֹ בַּחֲמִשִּׁים זוּז — יְכוֹלָה הִיא מִשֶּׁתַּגְדִּיל לְהוֹצִיא מִיָּדָן מַה שֶּׁרָאוּי לְהִנָּתֵן לָהּ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to a minor «orphan girl whose mother or brothers married her off,» even «with her consent» to a small dowry, she retains her rights to a proper dowry. «And» thus, if they «wrote for her» a dowry «of one hundred or of fifty dinars, she may, upon reaching majority, exact from» her mother, or brothers, or their respective estates the sum of money «that is fit to be given to her» as a dowry, which is one-tenth of the family’s estate. Even if she agreed to forgo part of this sum as a minor, she may collect it as an adult.

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם הִשִּׂיא אֶת הַבַּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה — יִנָּתֵן לַשְּׁנִיָּה כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנָּתַן לָרִאשׁוֹנָה. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם עָנִי וְהֶעֱשִׁיר, אוֹ עָשִׁיר וְהֶעֱנִי. אֶלָּא שָׁמִין אֶת הַנְּכָסִים וְנוֹתְנִין לָהּ.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yehuda says: If» the father «married off the first daughter» before he died, a dowry «should be given to the second» daughter «in the same manner that he gave» one «to the first» daughter. «And the Rabbis say:» There is no ready standard, since «sometimes a person» is «poor and» then «becomes wealthy, or» a person is «wealthy» and then «becomes poor,» so a family’s allowance for dowries is subject to change. «Rather,» the court «appraises the property and gives her» the appropriate sum.
